title: Test compatible parity bases from the actual local tables
statement: In the source generic ternary rank-two chart,reconstruct every eight-entry table,form edgeWfrom endpoint factors,and define eta_v,e=W10W11/(W00W01)at endpointv(with column analogue at the other end),R_v=(w_v1/w_v0)^2product_e eta_v,e. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field,compatible edge bases making every ternary tensor parity-homogeneous exist iffALLR_v=1. Real chart bases also need real edge square roots. R_vis invariant under rescaling and inverted under component exchange,soR_v=1is choice independent. The implementation builds bases and reconstructs entries exactly. R_v!=1rejects only this representation,not inference tractability; acquired nonzero fields may still be handled by actual face geometry.

assumptions: Generic recognition requires nondegenerate rank-two decompositions,invertible factor matrices/nonzero edge entries and exact supported field arithmetic. This is not a recognizer for arbitrary circuits/tensor networks. General boundary complexity charges the ACTUAL number of exposed faces and coefficient/field costs; planar embedding/cyclic order is supplied and checked. Original weights must be nonnegative with supported conditioning/positive totalmass; negative internal components are not probabilities. Rational/common-real-quadratic implementations do not silently handle arbitrary composita. The parent’s matched bucket-elimination implementation won tested instances; its earlier comparator was explicitly unavailable,so this is a parent comparison,not an independent review. No practical advantage or established novelty is claimed; P3remains visible-only.
costs: Recognition/basis reconstruction and all eight entries checked algebraically,not free supplied coordinates. Current executable arithmetic supports rationals and one common real quadratic field
